Team —

Thanks for routing. High-level legal guidance and proposed next steps / redlines for the MSA + Order Form negotiation (we should not make operational promises that the contract doesn't back up):

1) Immediate actions (operational):
- Preserve full request/response logs, model version, KV cache snapshots, and any associated customer metadata for 30 days (preservation period).
- We can offer a limited canary takedown of the specific outputs shown in the packet pending triage. We should avoid model-wide takedowns unless the evidence is compelling.

2) Notice & evidence requirements (contract redline):
- Require the customer to provide a written notice that includes: date/time of offending output(s), associated request IDs or session IDs, representative examples (no more than 10), and documentation substantiating ownership of the asserted IP.
- Add a chain-of-custody clause for evidence submissions (timestamped files, signer identity).

3) Indemnity scope & control of defense (contract redline options):
- Default position: Redwood offers indemnity for third-party IP claims alleging that our hosted service, when used as documented, directly reproduces third-party copyrighted code.
- Carveouts we should insist on: (a) no indemnity for claims based solely on customer prompt content (b) exclusions for open-source dependencies with existing OS licenses, (c) no indemnity where customer failed to provide required evidence or preserve logs.
- Defense control: prefer shared control — Redwood to lead defense for claims tied to our model infrastructure; customer may control settlement only with Redwood's written consent. If customer insists on full control, limit Redwood's monetary exposure and require customer's indemnity for settlement amounts that prejudice Redwood.

4) Caps, thresholds & remedies (contract redline):
- Cap liability for IP indemnity at the greater of (i) Order Form fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $2M.
- Deductible/retention: customer responsible for first $25k of defense costs for each claim if claim relates to customer prompts.
- Offer option: escrow holdback for enterprise deals > $1M ARR or attach insurance requirement (tech E&O with IP endorsement).

5) Operational SLAs for triage & escalation:
- Acknowledge notice within 24 hours (we already committed verbally).
- Provide preliminary triage within 72 hours (high/medium/low risk) and recommended mitigation.
- Full investigation (including forensics) target within 30 calendar days; if litigation, timeline may extend.

6) Evidence & data access (privacy/compliance):
- Limit the scope of data we provide to the minimum necessary to validate the claim; use a DPA-approved process for any user-level data.
- Any requests for training data or internal model weights: require a subpoena or court order unless previously agreed in the Order Form.

7) Next steps for negotiation:
- For the Order Form, propose a short indemnity appendix that references the MSA's core indemnity, defines notice/evidence steps, and includes the cap + optional escrow/insurance term.
- Ask ACME to accept our preservation steps and share the specific evidence (request IDs) so we can triage without overbroad takedowns.

I'll draft sample redline language this afternoon and drop it into the HubSpot deal. See internal playbook: https://internal.redwood/legal/playbooks/indemnity-ip (internal).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
